packageRules.description: One PR per dep — matches existing per-dependency Linear-ticket cadence

Pin Docker base image digests (UNK-254). Tags stay human-readable; the appended @sha256 digest gives tamper-evidence and reproducible buildkit cache behaviour. Scoped to Docker managers only — cargo/npm lockfiles already pin transitively. Digest bumps auto-merge via the auto-merge rule below: they stay libc-ABI-compatible within a Debian codename, and a sha256 bump cannot be meaningfully human-reviewed anyway (the reviewer cannot inspect layer contents from the digest). Note: minimumReleaseAge does NOT gate pin/digest update types (Renovate limitation), so digest bumps land within one schedule window with CI-green as the only check. Acceptable because all bases are Docker Official Images.

Auto-merge patch/pin/digest for Docker base images. Digest bumps cannot be meaningfully human-reviewed (the reviewer cannot inspect layer contents from a sha256) and all bases are Docker Official Images — see the pinDigests rule above for the full justification.

GitHub-owned actions (actions/*, github/*): auto-merge patch/pin/digest. Platform-trust tier — these share GitHub's own compromise boundary (if github.com itself is subverted, SHA-pinning does not save us), so a digest bump tracking first-party tag movement is auto-merged on CI-green, mirroring the Docker Official Images carve-out. Major/minor version bumps are absent here, so v6 -> v7 still requires manual review.

Third-party actions (dtolnay, dorny, Swatinem, taiki-e, docker/*, googleapis, …): auto-merge `pin` (tag -> its current SHA, no code change) and `patch` only. `digest` updates — a SHA-pinned tag re-pointed to new code — are deliberately NOT auto-merged and fall through to a manual PR. Unlike a Docker sha256, action source is human-reviewable, and these publishers do not share GitHub's trust boundary, so a digest bump is reviewed before it runs with the workflow GITHUB_TOKEN. This is the standing enforcement of the project's GitHub-Actions SHA-pinning policy.
Auto-merge patch updates for stable (v1.0.0+) cargo and npm dependencies. Pre-v1.0 (0.x.y) deps stay manual — SemVer isn't binding below 1.0 and Rust/npm 0.x patches can include behavioural changes

Pin rand_core_06 cargo alias at v0.6 — the alias name explicitly documents the deliberate version pin (v0.6 API is required by a transitive crypto consumer). Any bump silently breaks the pin intent and gets closed manually (see PR #122). Revisit if the alias is removed from Cargo.toml

vite-plus: one grouped PR for the setup-vp VP_VERSION pin and every npm token (the vite-plus devDependency, the vite alias, @voidzero-dev/*) so the ci.yml drift guard's lockstep holds. Placed last to win over the one-PR-per-dep rule for this dependency set.

customManagers.description: Rust-crate tools pinned inline via taiki-e/install-action `with: tool: <crate>@<ver>,<crate>@<ver>` syntax, plus the standalone cargo-deny pin in the audit job. install-action's manifest silently advances unpinned tools, so the project pins versions inline. Renovate's github-actions manager doesn't reach inside `with:` values, so without this manager those pins stay frozen. Tools are comma-joined in one `tool:` value, so the regex matches each `<crate>@<ver>` token by a hand-listed crate-name allowlist rather than anchoring on `tool:` — the anchor only ever preceded the first token and would leave later tools frozen. The allowlist keeps matches crate-scoped; sqlx-cli uses a different idiom — see the second manager.

sqlx-cli is pinned via a job-level SQLX_CLI_VERSION env var rather than install-action's `tool:` syntax (PR #288 moved it because install-action has no sqlx-cli manifest and was falling through to a 2-minute cargo install — the env var is now the single source of truth referenced by both the actions/cache key and the cargo install fallback). The env-var form doesn't match the `tool:` regex, so it needs its own manager. depNameTemplate hard-codes the crate name because the env-var name alone isn't crate-shaped.

Curl-installed lint binaries (actionlint + gitleaks are Go, shellcheck + hadolint are Haskell) are pinned by a `<TOOL>_VERSION` env var plus a `<TOOL>_SHA256` checksum the install step verifies. install-action carries none of them, so they live as direct curl-tarball installs and would otherwise freeze silently (UNK-327 repo-hygiene). Each version line carries a `# renovate:` inline annotation naming the github-releases datasource + repo; this manager reads those annotations so Renovate raises a bump PR when a new upstream release ships. CAVEAT: Renovate updates the VERSION token only — it cannot recompute a release-tarball SHA256, so the bump PR will red-X on the `sha256sum -c` check until a reviewer pastes the new checksum from the upstream release. That visible-failure is the intended outcome: a stale pin is now a loud PR instead of silent drift.

trufflehog's pinned Docker-image tag lives in a `with: version:` value, not a `<TOOL>_VERSION` env var, so neither Renovate's github-actions manager (which manages `uses:` refs but not their `with:` inputs) nor the curl-tarball manager above sees it. Left unmanaged it freezes while the action SHA advances, drifting the two out of lockstep. The inline `# renovate:` annotation names the github-releases datasource; extractVersion strips the leading `v` because the action's `version:` input wants the bare image tag (3.95.6, not v3.95.6). Same caveat applies as the curl pins: a bump PR updates only this token, so a reviewer must move the action SHA in the same PR to keep them in lockstep.
